facts.quote: In a nationwide design contest in 1989, the design of Suhail Abbasi & Naeem Pasha of M/s Suhail & Pasha, Architects & Planning Consultants Islamabad was selected for the construction of the National Art Gallery.

facts.fact: The design is a modernistic brick cube described as a model of Miesian purity and functionality.
facts.quote: Their modernistic brick cube is a model of Miesian purity and functionality.

facts.fact: It has 14 galleries with display areas, lecture halls, workshop and storage facilities, laboratories and a library.
facts.quote: The gallery, with a covered area of 1800 square yards, has 14 galleries with adjacent display areas, lecture halls, workshop and storage facilities, laboratories and a library.

facts.fact: The four-storey gallery includes a 400-seat auditorium, a theatre and an open-air theatre.
facts.quote: The four-storey gallery has modern facilities, including an auditorium with capacity for 400, a theatre, stage facilities and an open-air theatre.

facts.fact: It is a suspension bridge linking Olaya and Santa Fe de Antioquia across the Cauca River.
facts.quote: The Puente de Occidente (Bridge of the West), so named because it is located in western Antioquia, Colombia, is a suspension bridge that connects the municipalities of Olaya and Santa Fe de Antioquia, east and west of the Cauca River, respectively.

facts.fact: At the time it was considered the third largest suspension bridge in the world.
facts.quote: At the time it was considered to be the third largest suspension bridge worldwide.

facts.fact: A single suspension span hangs from four pyramidal towers, two on each bank, each anchoring two cables.
facts.quote: The bridge is a single suspension span supported from four pyramidal towers - two on each bank of the river - with each tower anchoring two cables.

facts.fact: A central section carries cars and smaller trucks, with a pedestrian path on each side.
facts.quote: The span has a main central section which cars and smaller trucks can cross, and two pedestrian paths on either side of the central roadway.

facts.fact: Construction began in 1887 under engineer José María Villa.
facts.quote: Construction started in 1887, under the direction of engineer José María Villa, after authorization by Marcelino Vélez, governor of Antioquia.

facts.fact: The cables and steel were bought from England while the towers used local materials.
facts.quote: The cables and other steel parts were purchased from England, while the towers were constructed of local materials.

facts.fact: Its structural system is similar to the suspension/cable-stayed hybrid of the Brooklyn Bridge.
facts.quote: The structural system of the Puente de Occidente is similar to the suspension/cable-stayed hybrid used in the Brooklyn Bridge.

facts.fact: It was declared a National Monument of Colombia on 26 November 1978.
facts.quote: It was declared a National Monument of Colombia on 26 November 1978.

facts.fact: It is a synagogue on the Hebrew University of Jerusalem's Mount Scopus campus.
facts.quote: is a synagogue located on the Mount Scopus campus of the Hebrew University of Jerusalem.

facts.fact: It is noted for the unique arrangement of the Torah ark and the panoramic view of the Old City from a huge window.
facts.quote: It is noted for the unique arrangement of the Torah ark and panoramic view of the Old City of Jerusalem from a huge window.

facts.fact: Israeli architect Ram Karmi designed it; construction finished in June 1981.
facts.quote: The building was designed by Israeli architect Ram Karmi.

facts.fact: The synagogue overlooks the Temple Mount.
facts.quote: The synagogue overlooks the Temple Mount.

facts.fact: It is built of Jerusalem stone, with a women's section on the gallery floor.
facts.quote: The building is constructed of Jerusalem stone with a women's section on the gallery floor.

facts.fact: It is Milan's main station and the largest railway station in Europe by volume.
facts.quote: is the main railway station of the city of Milan, Northern Italy, and is the second busiest railway station in Italy for passenger flow (after Roma Termini) and the largest railway station in Europe by volume.

facts.fact: It opened in 1931 to replace an 1864 station that could not handle traffic after the Simplon Tunnel opened.
facts.quote: It was officially inaugurated in 1931 to replace the old central station (built 1864), which was a transit station that could not handle the increased traffic caused by the opening of the Simplon Tunnel in 1906 due to the old station's limited number of tracks and space.

facts.fact: The station is a terminus at the northern end of central Milan.
facts.quote: The station is a terminus and located at the northern end of central Milan.

facts.fact: The king laid the cornerstone in 1906 before any blueprint had been chosen.
facts.quote: King Victor Emmanuel III of Italy laid the cornerstone of the new station on 28 April 1906, before a blueprint for the station had even been chosen.

facts.fact: Ulisse Stacchini won the last competition in 1912 with a project titled 'In Motu Vita', Latin for 'Life in Motion'.
facts.quote: The last, real, contest for its construction was won in 1912 by architect Ulisse Stacchini, who titled his project "In Motu Vita," meaning "Life in Motion" in Latin.

facts.fact: Its style was described as an eclectic mix called 'Assyrian-Lombard'.
facts.quote: The purported style was an eclectic mix called "Assyrian-Lombard."

facts.fact: Stacchini revised the project several times, mainly to address the city government's concerns about cost.
facts.quote: Stacchini made multiple revisions to the project, mainly to quell concerns by the Milan city government about high construction costs.

facts.fact: Alberto Fava's great steel canopies are 341 m long and cover 66,500 square metres.
facts.quote: The major changes were the new platform types and the introduction of the great steel canopies by Alberto Fava; 341 m (1,119 ft) long and covering an area of 66,500 square metres (716,000 sq ft).

facts.fact: Construction was very slow because of the economic crisis during World War I.
facts.quote: Due to the Italian economic crisis during World War I, construction proceeded very slowly.

facts.fact: The chapel was built and decorated between 1947 and 1951 under a plan devised by Henri Matisse.
facts.quote: The church was built and decorated between 1947 and 1951 under a plan devised by the artist Henri Matisse.

facts.fact: At 77, Matisse spent more than four years on its architecture, stained glass, murals, ceramics, furnishings and vestments.
facts.quote: At the age of 77, Matisse began the project and spent more than four years working on the chapel, its architecture, stained-glass windows, interior murals and ceramics, liturgical furnishings, and the priests' vestments.

facts.fact: Matisse regarded the chapel as his 'masterpiece'.
facts.quote: It houses a number of Matisse original works and was regarded by Matisse as his "masterpiece".

facts.fact: The chapel is built on a hillside and entered by descending a flight of stairs.
facts.quote: The chapel is built on a hillside and is entered by descending a flight of stairs, and turning to the right.

facts.fact: Its plan is an L shape with the longer portion directly inside the door.
facts.quote: The chapel is in an L shape, with the longer portion directly inside the door.

facts.fact: The altar sits at an angle where the two legs of the L join.
facts.quote: The altar is placed at an angle where the two legs of the L join.

facts.fact: The chapel is 15 meters long by 6 meters wide.
facts.quote: The chapel is 15 meters long by 6 meters wide.

facts.fact: Reactions to the simple white exterior are mixed, though some regard it as one of the great religious structures of the 20th century.
facts.quote: While the simple white exterior has drawn mixed reviews from casual observers, some regard it as one of the great religious structures of the 20th century.

facts.fact: The museum holds 3,125 works by Clyfford Still, 93 percent of his lifetime output.
facts.quote: The museum's collection includes 3,125 works by abstract expressionist Clyfford Still (1904–1980), which represents 93 percent of the artist's lifetime output and complete archives.

facts.fact: Still's will required his collection to go to a city willing to build a museum devoted only to his art.
facts.quote: When Clyfford Still died in 1980, his will stipulated that his entire collection be given to an American city willing to establish a permanent museum dedicated exclusively to the care and display of his art.

facts.fact: The board chose Allied Works Architecture, led by Brad Cloepfil, in 2006.
facts.quote: Later that year, the board selected Allied Works Architecture, led by Brad Cloepfil, for the museum’s design.

facts.fact: The site is in Denver's Civic Center Cultural Complex, west of the Denver Art Museum's Hamilton Building by Daniel Libeskind.
facts.quote: In 2006, the newly-formed Clyfford Still Museum secured a parcel of land within Denver's Civic Center Cultural Complex immediately west of the Denver Art Museum’s then-under-construction Frederic C. Hamilton Building, designed by Daniel Libeskind.

facts.fact: The 28,500-square-foot building has nine galleries, an art studio, visible painting storage, a conservation lab and two outdoor terraces.
facts.quote: The 28,500-square-foot building opened in 2011 and includes nine galleries, an art studio, visible painting storage areas and conservation lab, two outdoor terraces, archive displays, and outdoor forecourt green space.

facts.fact: Ground was broken in December 2009 and it opened on 18 November 2011.
facts.quote: The museum broke ground on its new home in December 2009 and opened to the public on November 18, 2011 as a single-artist museum.

facts.fact: The new basilica was designed by a group of architects including Pedro Ramírez Vázquez.
facts.quote: The new building was designed by the architects: José Luis Benlliure Galán, Pedro Ramírez Vázquez, Alejandro Schoenhofer, Friar Gabriel Chávez de la Mora, Antonio S. Gómez Palacio and Javier García Lascuráin.

facts.fact: It was built to house the image and admit more pilgrims, as the old temple was unstable and dangerous.
facts.quote: It was built due to the need to house the image of the Virgin of Guadalupe and allow access to a greater number of pilgrims, as the old temple was unstable and dangerous.

facts.fact: The old structure's subsidence and growing pilgrim numbers led to building the present basilica between 1974 and 1976.
facts.quote: Continuing subsidence in the old structure and the growing number of pilgrims led to the construction of the present basilica between 1974 and 1976.

facts.fact: The interior is circular and self-supporting, so the image can be seen from everywhere inside.
facts.quote: As the interior is circular and self-supporting (without supporting members to obstruct the view), the image of the Virgin of Guadalupe can be seen from everywhere inside the basilica.

facts.fact: A walkway with conveyor belts was built under the altar for better visibility of the image.
facts.quote: For better visibility of the image, a walkway was built under the altar with conveyor belts.

facts.fact: It was built on 344 control piles to prevent the land settling that affected surrounding buildings.
facts.quote: To prevent the settling of the land that occurred in surrounding buildings, this was built using 344 control piles, the work of engineer Manuel González Flores.

facts.fact: Seven entrances at the front sit below an open chapel recalling 16th-century atriums.
facts.quote: It has seven entrances to the front, above which there is an open chapel with a certain reminiscence of the atriums of the 16th century, from which mass can be celebrated for those present in the atrium.

facts.fact: The sanctuary receives some twenty million pilgrims a year.
facts.quote: Every year some twenty million pilgrims visit the sanctuary, of which about nine million do so in the days around December 12, the day on which Our Lady of Guadalupe is celebrated.

facts.fact: Kamran Diba designed it using elements of traditional Persian architecture from Yazd, Kashan and other desert towns.
facts.quote: The museum was designed by Iranian architect and cousin of the empress, Kamran Diba, who employed elements from traditional Persian architecture of Yazd, Kashan, and other desert towns.

facts.fact: Diba worked with architect Nader Ardalan during design.
facts.quote: Diba collaborated with architect Nader Ardalan during the design phase.

facts.fact: It stands beside Farah Park, now Laleh Park, and was inaugurated in 1977.
facts.quote: It was built adjacent to Farah Park, renamed Laleh Park after the Islamic revolution, and was inaugurated in 1977.

facts.fact: Most of the museum is underground, with a circular walkway spiralling down and galleries branching off.
facts.quote: Most of the museum area is located underground with a circular walkway that spirals downwards with galleries branching outwards.

facts.fact: It has been compared to an underground version of New York's Guggenheim Museum.
facts.quote: The building itself can be regarded as an example of contemporary art, in a style of an underground New York Guggenheim Museum.

facts.fact: The gardens hold Western sculptures by artists such as Ernst, Giacometti, Magritte and Moore.
facts.quote: Western sculptures by artists such as Ernst, Giacometti, Magritte, and Moore can be found in the museum's gardens.

facts.fact: After the 1979 revolution the Western art was stored in the vault until a 1999 exhibition.
facts.quote: After the Iranian Revolution in 1979, the Western art was stored away in the museum's vault until 1999 when the first post-revolution exhibition was held of western art showing artists such as David Hockney, Roy Lichtenstein, Robert Rauschenberg and Andy Warhol.

facts.fact: Architect Risto Šekerinski designed it, built from 1960 to 1963 next to the Orthodox Theology faculty.
facts.quote: It was designed by the architect Risto Šekerinski; started in 1960 and completed in 1963 it is located at 9 Mija Kovačević Street next to the Orthodox Theology, which is part of the University of Belgrade.

facts.fact: It is described as a brutalist skyscraper.
facts.quote: The brutalist skyscraper is located at 9 Mija Kovačević Street.

facts.fact: Locals call it Toblerone from the triangular shapes in its design.
facts.quote: deriving from the triangular shapes incorporated into the tower's design.

facts.fact: It is circular inside, with two elevators and triangular terraces.
facts.quote: The entire building is circular inside, has two elevators and triangular terraces.

facts.fact: It rises beside the Pančevo Bridge, which connects Serbia proper with Vojvodina.
facts.quote: It rises right next to the Pančevo Bridge, which connects Serbia proper with Vojvodina.

facts.fact: It won an architectural design award when it was built.
facts.quote: The building won an award for architectural design at the time of its construction.

facts.fact: It was conceived as a residential tower for Belgrade university.
facts.quote: in 1969, Toblerone had 104 connections installed, as this building was conceived as a residential tower for Belgrade university.

facts.fact: Meinhard von Gerkan and Nikolaus Goetze of Gerkan, Marg and Partners designed it.
facts.quote: The convention center was designed by Meinhard von Gerkan and Nikolaus Goetze of Gerkan, Marg and Partners.

facts.fact: Four designs were presented in April 2004.
facts.quote: Four designs were presented for consideration in April 2004.

facts.fact: A panel of 31 Vietnamese architects unanimously chose the design 'Surfing the East Sea'.
facts.quote: In the end, a design called "Surfing the East Sea" was unanimously chosen as the official design of the project by a panel of 31 Vietnamese architects.

facts.fact: The design takes inspiration from Hạ Long Bay.
facts.quote: The design of the center takes inspirations from Hạ Long Bay, a World Heritage Site in Quảng Ninh Province, Vietnam.

facts.fact: The wave-shaped steel roof rises to 53.25 m over the main meeting hall.
facts.quote: The building's wave-shaped roof is made from steel, heightened to 53.25 m (174.7 ft) over the main meeting hall.

facts.fact: The main structure is 215.25 m long and 113.5 m wide.
facts.quote: The main structure has a dimension of 215.25 m (706.2 ft) in length and 113.5 m (372 ft) in width.

facts.fact: Construction started on 15 November 2004 and it was inaugurated on 15 October 2006.
facts.quote: On 15 October 2006, the Vietnam National Convention Center was inaugurated.

facts.fact: It has solar panels as a back-up energy source.
facts.quote: It is equipped with solar power panels as a back-up energy source.

facts.fact: It is a museum in Hōki, Tottori, devoted solely to the photographer Shoji Ueda.
facts.quote: The Shoji Ueda Museum of Photography, is a museum in Hōki, Tottori, Japan that is solely dedicated to exhibiting and archiving the work of the photographer Shoji Ueda.

facts.fact: The museum was founded in 1995.
facts.quote: The museum was founded in 1995.

facts.fact: Shin Takamatsu designed the building.
facts.quote: The building was designed by Shin Takamatsu.

facts.fact: Volumes and voids, as scaled incisions in the volume, frame Mount Daisen.
facts.quote: The architectural relationships between volumetric solids and voids (as scaled incisions in the volume) function to frame Mount Daisen.

facts.fact: The collection has over 12,000 works by Ueda.
facts.quote: The collection consists of over 12,000 works by Shoji Ueda.
